coverage_note: Reviewed against official central-bank releases and policy accounts available by 27 November 2026. Rates and operating frameworks differ. A policy-tone label is an editorial assessment, not a market-implied rate forecast. The next-meeting dates are scheduled dates and should be rechecked if a bank changes its calendar.

methodology.stance: Hawkish / neutral / dovish describes the communication and balance of risks, not simply whether the last decision was a hike or hold.
methodology.next_direction: A conditional directional assessment, not a promise or market pricing. Update after decisions, minutes, forecasts and material governor communications.
methodology.relative: Pair comparison is ordinal and qualitative. A firmer tone supports a currency only if it is more hawkish than expected and than its counterpart; it is not a trade signal.
methodology.refresh: This snapshot is manually curated. The dashboard does not yet automatically interpret new speeches or minutes. Review daily and refresh after material policy communication.

central_banks.name: Federal Reserve
central_banks.next_direction: Further hike remains a live risk
central_banks.summary: The Committee held rates, but the October minutes showed broad support for further tightening under the baseline outlook; two members preferred a 25 bp increase at the meeting. Inflation remained elevated. This is a hawkish hold, not a rate increase.

central_banks.name: European Central Bank
central_banks.summary: The October account, published 26 November, says a large number of members could have supported a hike at the meeting; some argued a further increase was warranted unless the inflation outlook improved significantly. The Council nevertheless held at 2.50% and remains meeting-by-meeting. This is materially more hawkish than a plain neutral hold.

central_banks.name: Bank of England
central_banks.next_direction: Further tightening conditional on inflation pass-through
central_banks.summary: The MPC raised Bank Rate by 25 bp. The November report says UK CPI inflation reached 3.5% in September and is expected to rise further; higher energy prices and stronger activity supported the increase. The Committee stressed that policy is not on a pre-set path.

central_banks.name: Bank of Japan
central_banks.summary: The BOJ maintained its call-rate guideline around 1.25%. Its October outlook and board discussion point to continued normalisation as its outlook is realised; one board member proposed 1.50%. The pace remains conditional on wages, prices and activity.
central_banks.source_name: BOJ official policy releases and October outlook

central_banks.name: Swiss National Bank
central_banks.next_direction: Hold likely; FX intervention remains available
central_banks.summary: The SNB held at 0%. It judged policy appropriate for price stability and economic development; medium-term inflation pressure had increased only slightly. It remains willing to intervene in foreign exchange markets when necessary.

central_banks.name: Bank of Canada
central_banks.summary: The Bank raised its overnight rate by 25 bp to 2.50%. It said inflation is higher and more persistent than previously projected and that another increase may be needed, while emphasising a careful, data-dependent approach.
central_banks.source_name: Bank of Canada policy decision · 28 October

central_banks.name: Reserve Bank of Australia
central_banks.next_direction: Further tightening risk if inflation stays broad-based
central_banks.summary: The RBA raised the cash rate by 25 bp to 4.85%. Six members voted to increase and three preferred a hold. Inflation was broad-based, capacity pressures remained tight and the Board judged tighter financial conditions warranted.

central_banks.name: Reserve Bank of New Zealand
central_banks.next_direction: Hold while assessing inflation and uneven recovery
central_banks.summary: The RBNZ maintained the OCR at 2.75%. Inflation is above target, largely reflecting global fuel costs, while the recovery remains gradual and uneven. The Bank says it will adjust the OCR as needed to return inflation to 2%.
central_banks.source_name: RBNZ official cash rate · updated 28 October
